specPoints.text: explain the detrimental effects of excessive exposure of the human body to electromagnetic waves, including: • microwaves: internal heating of body tissue

primer.text: The same spectrum that carries phone calls and photographs can damage the body that receives them. Frequency is the lever: beyond the visible band the energy of each wave grows large enough to ionise atoms, and the hazards climb with it. This lesson matches each band to its danger and to the simple measures that cut the risk.

lessons.title: Dangers of EM waves & protective measures
sourceHeadings: Dangers and uses of each part of the EM spectrum
Protective measures against the risks of over-exposure
lessons.opening: Over-exposure harms by band: microwaves heat tissue inside the body, infrared burns the skin, ultraviolet damages surface cells and can blind, and gamma with x-rays can trigger cancer and mutation. Against these, engineers and clinicians build simple barriers: metal oven walls, gloves, sunglasses and sunscreen, minimal doses and badge-monitored exposure.
keyPoints: Microwaves can cause internal heating of body tissue.
Ultraviolet can damage surface cells and cause blindness.
Gamma rays and x-rays can kill cells, causing cancer and mutation.
Protective measures include metal oven walls, protective gloves, sunglasses, sunscreen, minimal doses and radiation badges.

low.restatement: Each hazardous band has a named harm and a simple counter: heating against microwaves, burns against infrared, cell damage against ultraviolet, cancer risk against gamma and x-ray.
low.analogy: Sun etiquette scaled up: shade, clothing and cream are the same logic engineers apply to every band.
low.examPointer: Learn the band-to-harm list verbatim; matching the wrong harm to a band loses the mark even if the protection is right.

medium.restatement: The danger climbs with frequency because photon energy does: past visible, radiation ionises atoms, so the short-wavelength bands break molecular bonds in cells while the long bands merely heat them.
medium.analogy: A hierarchy of tools: a hairdryer warms you, a UV lamp burns, an x-ray machine cuts at the molecular level.
medium.examPointer: When asked to explain the trend, say energy increases with frequency and ionisation begins beyond visible; that chain earns the reasoning mark.

check.stem: Excessive exposure to microwaves is dangerous because microwaves:

options.explanation: Surface burns are the infrared hazard.
Blindness is the ultraviolet hazard.
Microwaves deposit energy as internal heating of tissue.
That is the gamma and x-ray hazard.
Infrared over-exposure burns the skin.
Radio is the low-energy communications band.
X-ray hazard is cell damage and cancer risk.
Microwaves heat tissue internally rather than browning skin.

check.stem: Ultraviolet over-exposure can damage surface cells and also cause:

options.explanation: Internal heating is the microwave hazard.
Ultraviolet damages the eyes as well as skin cells.
That is not a listed ultraviolet effect.
That is irrelevant to the human-body harm list.

check.stem: Gamma rays and x-rays are hazardous because they can:

options.explanation: Gentle heating is a mild effect far below their real hazard.
The hazard list is about the human body.
Sunburn is the ultraviolet effect.

options.text: kill cells, causing cancer and mutation
options.explanation: Cell death from these ionising radiations leads to cancer and mutation risks.

check.stem: The harm from ultraviolet, gamma and x-ray exposure increases with frequency because:

options.explanation: All EM waves share one speed in free space.

options.text: higher-frequency waves carry more energy and can ionise atoms
options.explanation: Energy rises with frequency, and ionisation begins beyond visible.
Loudness is a sound property, irrelevant here.

options.text: lower-frequency waves are blocked by air
options.explanation: The trend runs with frequency, not with air blocking.

check.stem: State the harm caused by excessive exposure to infrared radiation.
State two protective measures against ultraviolet exposure.
check.modelAnswer: Wear sunglasses that absorb ultraviolet, and apply sunscreen that absorbs ultraviolet before it damages the skin.

check.stem: Explain why radiographers leave the room during x-ray imaging and wear radiation badges.
check.modelAnswer: X-rays are ionising, so repeated daily exposure would raise their cumulative dose and cancer risk; leaving the room avoids unnecessary exposure and the badge measures the dose they do receive so it can be checked and limited.

check.stem: A microwave oven protects its user with metal walls and a metal grid in the door. Explain how this works and name the harm it prevents.
check.modelAnswer: The metal surfaces reflect and contain the microwaves so they cannot escape the cavity, preventing the internal heating of body tissue that excessive microwave exposure would cause.

glossary.definition: To remove electrons from atoms, producing charged particles; ionising radiation can damage living cells.
A badge worn by radiation workers that records the dose of radiation received.
Exposure to radiation beyond the safe dose — the shared cause of every harm on this lesson's list.
